title: The Earth as a System
summary: The Earth's four spheres and how they interact, the structure of the Earth, the rock cycle and the three types of rock.

notes.text: The Earth is a **system** made up of four interacting parts, or **spheres**. A change in one sphere affects the others.

rows: Lithosphere
The solid rocky outer layer: the crust and the top of the mantle, rocks and soil
Hydrosphere
All the water on Earth: oceans, rivers, lakes, groundwater, ice and water vapour
Atmosphere
The layer of gases surrounding the Earth
Biosphere
All living organisms and the places where they live

notes.title: Spheres interacting
notes.problem: Explain how a volcanic eruption affects the other spheres.
steps: Lithosphere: lava and ash form new rock and land.
Atmosphere: gases and ash are released, which can block sunlight and cool the climate.
Hydrosphere: ash pollutes rivers; gases dissolve in rain to form acid rain.
Biosphere: plants and animals are killed or lose their habitats, but volcanic soil later becomes very fertile.
notes.answer: One event in the lithosphere changes all four spheres.

notes.label: Remember
notes.text: The **water cycle** links the spheres: water evaporates from the hydrosphere into the atmosphere, falls as rain on the lithosphere, and is used by the biosphere (plants transpire water back into the air).

rows: Crust
Thin, solid outer layer of rock: 5 to 10 km thick under oceans, up to 70 km under mountains
Mantle
Thick layer of hot rock; the upper part moves very slowly like a thick paste
Outer core
Liquid iron and nickel; its movement produces the Earth's magnetic field
Inner core
Solid iron and nickel at about 5 500 °C; solid because of the huge pressure

notes.text: The crust and upper mantle are broken into large pieces called **tectonic plates**, which move a few centimetres per year. Earthquakes, volcanoes and mountain-building happen mainly along plate boundaries.

rows: Igneous
Molten rock (magma or lava) cools and hardens. Slow cooling underground gives large crystals; fast cooling at the surface gives small crystals.
Granite (slow), basalt (fast)
Sedimentary
Weathered fragments (sediments) are carried by water or wind, deposited in layers, compacted and cemented together
Sandstone, shale, limestone; coal forms from plant remains
Metamorphic
Existing rock is changed by great heat and pressure underground, without melting
Marble (from limestone), slate (from shale), quartzite (from sandstone)

notes.text: **Fossils**, the preserved remains or traces of ancient organisms, are found mostly in sedimentary rock. The Karoo is famous for fossils of reptiles and early mammal-like animals.

Rocks are constantly changed from one type into another over millions of years:

**weathering and erosion → transport → deposition → compaction and cementation (sedimentary rock) → heat and pressure (metamorphic rock) → melting (magma) → cooling (igneous rock) → uplift and weathering again**

notes.text: The breaking down of rock in place by the weather, plant roots or chemicals.
The wearing away and carrying away of rock fragments by water, wind or ice.

notes.title: A grain of sand's journey
notes.problem: Granite in a mountain ends up as quartzite. Describe the steps and name the rock types.
steps: Granite is **igneous**. Weathering breaks it into sand, which rivers carry to the sea.
Layers of sand are compacted and cemented into sandstone, a **sedimentary** rock.
Great heat and pressure deep underground change the sandstone into quartzite, a **metamorphic** rock.

questions.prompt: Which sphere includes all the water on Earth?
Soil and rocks belong to the…
Why is the inner core solid even though it is extremely hot?
options: It is cooled by the mantle

questions.prompt: What type of rock is granite?
Fossils are mainly found in sedimentary rocks.
Match each metamorphic rock to the rock it formed from.
Explain why granite has large crystals but basalt has small crystals.
questions.memo:
✓ Granite forms from magma cooling slowly underground, giving crystals time to grow (1)
✓ Basalt forms from lava cooling quickly at the surface, so crystals stay small (1)

✓ Rocks are weathered and eroded into small fragments (1)
✓ The sediments are transported and deposited in layers (1)
✓ Over time the layers are compacted and cemented together (1)

questions.prompt: Give an example of the biosphere interacting with the lithosphere.
questions.memo: ✓✓ Any valid example with explanation, e.g. plant roots growing into cracks break rocks apart (biological weathering); earthworms mix soil; decomposers add nutrients to soil

questions.prompt: What is the difference between weathering and erosion?
questions.memo:
✓ Weathering breaks rock down where it is (1)
✓ Erosion carries the broken pieces away (by water, wind or ice) (1)
